value.title: Three dora and an 8-tile wait, kept dama

text.situation: East 2, turn 8. You are the dealer, fourth at 22,700. You draw [[4p]] into tenpai: cut [[7s]] and you wait on [[5m]]-[[8m]] with 8 tiles live. The hand is tanyao with three [[2m]] as dora. Nobody has declared. Kamicha has ponned [[C]] and [[F]].
text.did: You cut [[7s]] and stayed dama. The hand won by tsumo for 12,000.
text.luckyj: LuckyJ declares 95% of first closed tenpais with 8 or more live tiles before turn 10. Two dragon pons across the table do not stop it: in the 22 hands where an opponent already showed two dragon pons, it still declared 16 times, including all 3 with 8 or more live tiles. That sample is small.
text.fix: Declare. Dama caps this hand at a dealer mangan, 12,000, on ron or tsumo. Riichi makes the same tsumo a haneman, 18,000, and gives a ron the same chance through ura dora and ippatsu. The cost is having to cut a drawn haku [[P]] into the two dragon pons. LuckyJ wins about 60% of its riichi hands with 8 or more live tiles.

value.title: Pinfu on an 8-tile wait at turn 6, kept dama

text.situation: South 2, two honba, turn 6. You are third at 19,100. You draw [[1s]] and reach tenpai: cut [[7p]] and you wait on [[5s]]-[[8s]], 8 tiles live. The hand is pinfu and nothing else. The dealer has ponned [[S]]; nobody has declared.
text.did: You stayed dama. The hand won by tsumo for 2,100.
text.luckyj: LuckyJ declares 95% of first closed tenpais with 8 or more live tiles before turn 10.
text.fix: Riichi. Before the honba, dama pays 1,000 on a ron and 1,500 on a tsumo. Riichi pays 2,000 and 2,700, before ura dora. A one-han hand on a two-sided wait at turn 6 is the hand riichi exists for.

calls.title: The better tile was also the safer one

text.situation: South 1, turn 6. Kamicha, leading with 46,000, has ponned haku [[P]]. You are third at 21,500, 3-shanten with two dora, and draw [[2m]].
text.did: You cut the [[2m]] you drew. It left 36 tiles of acceptance and was live against the pon. It dealt in for 1,000.
text.fix: [[S]] leaves 38 tiles and has two other copies showing, so only a tanki can hit it. When the safer tile is also the more efficient one, it is the only cut.

calls.title: Turn 13, a free honor in hand

text.situation: South 1, turn 13 with 18 tiles left. Kamicha, leading with 36,700, has ponned [[3p]]. You are third at 18,300 and 1-shanten after a closed kan of [[1p]].
text.did: You cut the [[7m]] you drew, live against the pon, and dealt in for 3,900.
text.luckyj: When a safe tile keeps the same shanten and acceptance against a single call, LuckyJ takes it 83% of the time at 1-shanten from turn 13 on.
text.fix: [[C]] leaves the same 12 tiles and has two other copies showing. Take it.

text.situation: South 4, turn 9. You and toimen are tied for first at 33,600. The dealer, third at 23,500, has ponned haku [[P]]. You are 1-shanten with a chi and two red fives.
text.did: You cut the [[9m]] you drew, live against the dealer, and paid 1,500. The dealer's win also kept the game going.
text.luckyj: Against a single call LuckyJ takes a free safe tile 69% of the time at 1-shanten on turns 9 to 12.
text.fix: [[N]] leaves the same 6 tiles and has two other copies showing. In all last with first place on the line, a free safe tile is never optional.

calls.title: 8,000 from a tile that was not even the most efficient

text.situation: East 1, turn 7. Toimen ponned [[N]], their seat wind, then added the fourth [[N]] as a kan, and has kept cutting tiles from hand since. You are 2-shanten with a pair of [[F]] and two dora.
text.did: You cut [[4m]], only half suji against the kan because just the [[7m]] side was covered, leaving 20 tiles of acceptance, and dealt in for 8,000.
text.luckyj: Against a single call, LuckyJ pays one or two tiles of acceptance for a safe tile about a quarter of the time. Here the safe tile cost nothing against the tile you chose.
text.fix: [[F]] leaves 21 tiles, one more than [[4m]]. With your other [[F]] and the one in kamicha's river, only a tanki on the last copy can hit it. [[8m]] and [[2p]] leave 22 but are live too. A kan of a value wind is a hand with its yaku done: take the honor.

text.situation: South 3, one honba, turn 11. The dealer has ponned [[3m]]. You are fourth at 19,300, 2-shanten, with a [[2s]] pon and the dora, haku [[P]].
text.did: You cut [[3p]], live, leaving 10 tiles. On the next turn no safe tile kept the hand, and [[2p]] dealt in for 1,800.
text.fix: [[4s]] is genbutsu and leaves 14 tiles, because three [[2s]] sit in your own pon and the fourth is in the dealer's river, so [[3s]][[4s]] can only take [[5s]]. [[E]] is genbutsu with 14 as well. Count a shape's live tiles before you protect it.

calls.title: Two pons across the table and a live honor

text.situation: South 1, turn 8. You are the dealer, second at 21,500, and you have just ponned haku [[P]]. Toimen has ponned [[S]], the round wind, and [[5m]] with the red five.
text.did: After the pon you cut [[C]], an honor with no other copy showing, and dealt in for 2,000. Toimen was waiting on it alone.
text.luckyj: Against two calls LuckyJ cuts a live tile only about 30% of the time from turn 9 on when a safe tile keeps its shanten.
text.fix: [[8p]] is genbutsu and leaves 41 tiles against 43. A hand built from pons often ends on a tanki or a shanpon, so a live honor is one of the likeliest tiles to hit it. Pay the two tiles.

calls.title: Twelve discards and not one sou

text.situation: South 2, turn 12. You lead with 43,300. Shimocha, last at 6,300, has ponned [[F]] and chied [[2s]][[3s]][[4s]], and has discarded twelve tiles without a single sou. You are open tenpai on a [[6m]] kanchan and draw [[9s]].
text.did: You cut the [[9s]] and dealt in for 7,700 to a sou honitsu.
text.fix: A dragon pon, a sou chi and a river with no sou is a honitsu, and its waits are sou. Fold with the red [[5mr]], genbutsu. It costs the tenpai and a red five from a 3-han hand. With an 11,000-point lead, the deal-in costs more.

folds.title: The tile that was safe against both players

frames.note: Kamicha has just discarded [[2p]], so [[2p]] is now genbutsu against both players. [[3s]] is safe against the riichi, because toimen passed it after the declaration, and live against kamicha's pon.
[[1s]] is genbutsu against kamicha and only suji against the riichi. [[2p]] is still genbutsu against both.

text.situation: East 4, one honba. You lead with 40,800. Shimocha declared riichi on turn 4 and kamicha has ponned haku [[P]]. You are folding at 2-shanten.
text.did: You cut [[3s]] on turn 12 and [[1s]] on turn 13. The [[1s]] completed shimocha's shanpon for 1,600.
text.luckyj: At 2-shanten against a riichi, LuckyJ keeps a safe tile 96% of the time when one holds its shanten. You already fold that often. The leak here is which safe tile.
text.fix: Rank the safe tiles before you cut: genbutsu against every threat, then genbutsu against the riichi, then an honor with two other copies showing, then suji, with a 1 or 9 on suji the safest of those. Suji only rules out a two-sided wait; shanpon, tanki and kanchan still hit it. [[2p]] topped that list for two turns and cost two or three tiles of acceptance in a hand that was folding anyway.

folds.title: The safe tile that also kept the better hand

text.situation: East 1, turn 10. Shimocha declared riichi on the turn before. You are second at 25,000, 2-shanten with two dora ([[F]] and the red [[5pr]]) and a pair of [[N]].
text.did: You broke the [[N]] pair. No other [[N]] is showing, so a shanpon or tanki on it is still possible, and it left 20 tiles of acceptance.
text.fix: [[2m]] is genbutsu and leaves 43 tiles. When a safe tile is also the better tile for the hand, there is nothing to weigh.

text.situation: East 2, one honba, turn 13 with 23 tiles left. You are the dealer and lead with 34,700. Toimen declared riichi on turn 6 and kamicha has ponned [[F]]. You are 2-shanten.
text.did: You cut [[8p]], live against both players, to keep 2-shanten.
text.luckyj: At 2-shanten on turn 13 or later, LuckyJ cuts a live tile against a riichi 5.0% of the time.
text.fix: Fold with [[7s]], suji against both players, or [[3p]], genbutsu against both. Either costs a shanten. From 2-shanten with about five draws left the hand rarely reaches tenpai at all, so that shanten was worth little, and a leading dealer has more to lose from a deal-in than from a folded hand.

folds.title: Genbutsu against the riichi that also kept more tiles

text.situation: South 1, one honba, turn 16 with 6 tiles left. Kamicha declared riichi on turn 11, shimocha has two calls and toimen one. You are third at 20,100 and 2-shanten.
text.did: You cut [[5s]]: nakasuji against the riichi, and only half suji against the two open hands, which both hold sou melds.
text.luckyj: Against one riichi, LuckyJ's nakasuji cuts dealt into it 2.8 times per 100 and its genbutsu never did.
text.fix: [[3p]] is genbutsu against the riichi and leaves more acceptance, 32 tiles against 26. Neither tile is safe against the open hands. [[7p]] is suji against all three players, but it is a 3-7 suji, the weakest kind, against the riichi.

folds.title: Two riichis: check the tile against both

text.situation: South 2, one honba, turn 16 with 7 tiles left. Shimocha and kamicha are both in riichi. You are second at 23,400 and 1-shanten.
text.did: You cut [[8m]]: genbutsu against kamicha, live against shimocha.
text.luckyj: When a safe tile leaves exactly the same shanten and acceptance, LuckyJ pushes past it about 2% of the time at 1-shanten.
text.fix: [[6m]] is genbutsu against both riichis and leaves the same 10 tiles. With two riichis, check every tile against each river separately.

text.situation: South 3, turn 10. Kamicha declared riichi on turn 4. You are third at 24,500, open with two chis and a concealed [[F]] triplet, and you draw the red [[5sr]].
text.did: You cut [[6m]], genbutsu, and gave up the tenpai.
text.luckyj: With an open tenpai against a riichi, where keeping it needs a dangerous tile, LuckyJ pushes 93% of the time with 8 or more live tiles, and 91% of the time when such a hand is only 1 or 2 han.
text.fix: Cut the red [[5sr]] and wait on [[5m]]-[[8m]] with 8 tiles. It costs a han and leaves [[F]] and the red [[5pr]], about 2,000 points. An 8-tile wait with a yaku is the tenpai you push.

push.title: A tenpai that could not win by ron

text.situation: South 2, turn 14 with 14 tiles left. Kamicha has just declared riichi and shimocha has ponned [[4s]]. You are fourth at 20,800 and draw [[3p]] into tenpai.
text.did: You cut [[2s]], live against the riichi, to wait on [[4s]]. The hand has no yaku, so it could only win by tsumo, and three [[4s]] were already in shimocha's pon: one tile in the whole game could complete it. The [[2s]] dealt in for 8,000.
text.luckyj: LuckyJ pushes 43% of its tenpai hands against a riichi, you 38%. What decides the push is the yaku: LuckyJ pushes 86% of its open tenpais that have a yaku on the wait, and 55% of those with none.
text.fix: Fold with [[2p]], genbutsu against the riichi and suji against shimocha. Cutting the red [[5sr]] for a [[1s]]-[[4s]] wait does not help: all four [[1s]] are gone. A yakuless dama with one live tile is worth about as much as a 1-shanten hand.
